transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health suggested I come in. I guess… I’ve got into a habit of skipping, or pushing off, breakfast and lunch when I’m busy with lab runs or exhibition work. And then when I do eat, I tend to keep it quite small. Controlled, I suppose.
Do you find yourself not wanting to eat when you skip breakfast and lunch?
I wouldn’t say I don’t want to eat exactly… I just push it aside when I’m busy, and then later I keep it small. It feels easier if it’s controlled.
Have you lost any weight recently?

A bit, yes. My clothes are looser, and the number on the scale has… kept going down. I suppose part of me hasn’t seen it as a bad thing. More like I’m staying focused, keeping things contained when work feels chaotic.
Is losing weight something you've been trying to do?

Not exactly in a… formal way. I suppose I’ve just got into this pattern of pushing breakfast and lunch aside when I’m busy, and then when I do eat, keeping it very small. Controlled. So… maybe, in a way, yes.
Do you think your weight loss is a good thing?

I mean… I don’t really see it as a serious problem. I know people are concerned, but I’m still getting through work, doing my experiments. So it feels a bit overstated, honestly. I don’t feel like I’m in any medical danger.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
I… yes, I suppose I am. If the scale goes up even a tiny bit, I get this sudden panic, like I’ve let things slip… like I’m losing the discipline I’ve been trying to keep.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you try to control your food intake?
Yes… I think so. It’s not the only thing I tell myself, but when the scale goes up even a little, I get this sharp panic. Like I’m losing the discipline I’ve worked hard to keep.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?
I think it’s… probably not as bad as everyone’s making it sound. I know people are worried, but I’m still working, still doing my experiments. I don’t feel like I’m in any real medical danger.
Do you feel like you would be happier if you were thinner?

I… I think I would, yes. Or at least I think I’d feel less distracted by it. When I look in the mirror before going to the lab, I don’t really see someone thin. I just notice my stomach or my hips and think they make me look… careless, I guess. Not serious.
Do you often think about your weight or body shape when deciding what or how much to eat?

Yes. I mean… I try to tell myself it’s just practical, but if I’ve looked in the mirror and noticed my stomach or my hips, it affects what I’ll let myself eat. It makes me feel like I look careless, or not serious enough.
Do you feel like eating a normal or large amount of food would make you feel like you're losing control?
I suppose… yes, a bit. I’ve gotten into this pattern where I put off breakfast and lunch when I’m busy in the lab, and then when I do eat, I keep it very small. It feels more… controlled that way.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period?
No… I don’t think so. Not definitely larger. If anything, I usually stop before it gets to that point.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that feels excessive to you, even if it's not necessarily more than what most people would eat?
Sometimes it feels like too much to me, yes… but I don’t know if that’s the same thing. It can be a pretty normal amount, I suppose. I just… feel uncomfortable with it.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that is excessive to you, and then tried to compensate for it by restricting your food intake or purging?

I don’t purge. I just… if I feel I’ve had too much, I tend to make the next meals smaller, or skip them if I’m caught up in lab work. Occupational health noticed, I think… breakfast and lunch get pushed aside, and then I keep whatever I do eat very small.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?
No. I… I haven’t made myself vomit.
Do you ever use exercise to try to compensate for eating what feels like too much to you?
I… I don’t really think of it that way. I mean, I do try to stay active, but I’m not sure I’d call it compensating. It’s hard to say.
Do you ever use laxatives to try to compensate for eating what feels like too much to you?
No… I don’t use laxatives for that.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?
I don’t think so… not like a really large amount. I mean, sometimes I feel uncomfortable after eating, but I wouldn’t say I can’t stop.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is what primarily drives your decision to restrict your food intake?
Yes… I think so. I don’t like admitting that, but if the scale goes up even a little, I feel this sudden panic, like I’m losing control or the discipline I’ve worked hard to keep.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?
I’m not sure… I don’t really think of it that way. Sometimes I feel bad after eating, but “lost control” feels… stronger than what I’d say.
